messages.subject: rxnNorm Demo
parts:
Good Morning all... Several have asked for the code to make these plots, so the code and a test case that produces the attached plots are attached (thanks for the interest).

I collaborate with an ecologist and we are working on plant stress, studying different levels of stress and different genotypes of a plant.  In ecology they like to create plots like the ones shown to see if there is a genotype x stress effect, which is evidenced by non-parallel or crossing lines.  In these plots, the response is on the y axis, the stress (either categorical or numerical) is on the x axis, and the different sets of lines are the genotypes.  Of course, this could be adapted in a number of ways for similar purposes.

You’ll note that the boxplot option executes but doesn’t give quite what is expected.  If anyone sees what’s wrong with it, I’d love to know.  Everything else seems to work OK.

Also, the stat_summary functions I call are from my ChemoSpec package available at http://github.com/bryanhanson/ChemoSpec.  Any function you write that returns a measure of central tendency and two extremes will work, it just has to return 3 values to stat_summary.

Have fun.  Suggestions welcome.  Bryan
*************
Bryan Hanson
Acting Chair
Professor of Chemistry & Biochemistry
DePauw University, Greencastle IN USA

Hi,

I'm playing around with this and I do not manage to create an annotation table
that is annotates the facets of a facet_wrap.

Based on a ggplot2 documentation example I build

d <- ggplot(
diamonds,
aes(carat, price, fill = ..density..)
)

d <- d +
xlim(0, 2) +
stat_binhex(na.rm = TRUE) +
opts(aspect.ratio = 1)

# Annotation table with "color" column
myTable <- data.frame(
Some=rep(1,length(levels(diamonds[["color"]]))),
Thing=rep(2,length(levels(diamonds[["color"]]))),
color=unique(diamonds[["color"]])
)

d + facet_wrap(~ color) + annotate("table",0.25,17500,table=myTable)

Can I get the annotation table faceted according to "color"?

Thanks, Joh
